ETC is the abbreviation for the Electronic Toll Collection system on highways, which can speed up the passage of vehicles on highways. As shown in the figure, vehicles 1 and 2 both start with an initial velocity of $v_{0}=15\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ and travel in the same direction, taking the ETC lane and the manual toll lane respectively to exit the highway. Vehicle 1 starts to decelerate uniformly from the deceleration line AB, and when its speed reduces to $v=5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$, it continues to travel at a constant speed to the centerline of the toll station, then accelerates uniformly back to $15\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ before exiting. Vehicle 2 also starts to decelerate uniformly from the deceleration line AB, comes to a complete stop exactly at the centerline of the toll station, spends $10\mathrm{s}$ paying the toll, and then accelerates uniformly back to $15\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ before exiting. It is known that both vehicles have an acceleration and deceleration magnitude of $2.5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. During the process of a car passing through the toll station, the distance traveled at a constant speed is...
2. Both cars decelerate from $15\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ and then accelerate back to a speed of exactly $15\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. Car 1 uses less time than Car 2 during this process.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: There are two driving lanes in the figure, and the vehicles are both traveling to the right. The blue vertical dashed line on the left passes through A and B, representing the deceleration line AB where the two vehicles jointly begin to decelerate; the blue vertical dashed line on the right represents the toll station centerline. object 1 is in ETC Lane, and object 2 is in Manual toll lane. Then reason: First use vehicle 2 to determine the distance from deceleration line AB to the toll station centerline. Vehicle 2 uniformly decelerates from 15 m/s to 0, with a deceleration magnitude of 2.5 m/s². From v² - v0² = 2as, taking the direction of motion as positive, a = -2.5 m/s²: 0² - 15² = 2(-2.5)s, so s = 45 m. Vehicle 1 uniformly decelerates from 15 m/s to 5 m/s, with the same deceleration magnitude of 2.5 m/s². From 5² - 15² = 2(-2.5)s, obtain s = 40 m. Therefore, after vehicle 1 decelerates to 5 m/s, the remaining distance to the toll station centerline is 45 - 40 = 5 m, and this section is the uniform-speed driving distance. Calculate time: The deceleration time of vehicle 1 is (15 - 5)/2.5 = 4 s, the time to pass 5 m at uniform speed is 5/5 = 1 s, and the time to accelerate from 5 m/s to 15 m/s is (15 - 5)/2.5 = 4 s, so the total time for vehicle 1 is 4 + 1 + 4 = 9 s. The time for vehicle 2 to decelerate to a stop is 15/2.5 = 6 s, the toll payment stop is 10 s, and the time to accelerate to 15 m/s is 15/2.5 = 6 s, so the total time for vehicle 2 is 6 + 10 + 6 = 22 s. Vehicle 1 uses 22 - 9 = 13 s less time than vehicle 2.

ETC is the abbreviation for the Electronic Toll Collection system on highways, which can speed up the passage of vehicles on highways. As shown in the figure, vehicles 1 and 2 both start with an initial velocity of $v_{0}=15\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ and travel in the same direction, taking the ETC lane and the manual toll lane respectively to exit the highway. Vehicle 1 starts to decelerate uniformly from the deceleration line AB, and when its speed reduces to $v=5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$, it continues to travel at a constant speed to the centerline of the toll station, then accelerates uniformly back to $15\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ before exiting. Vehicle 2 also starts to decelerate uniformly from the deceleration line AB, comes to a complete stop exactly at the centerline of the toll station, spends $10\mathrm{s}$ paying the toll, and then accelerates uniformly back to $15\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ before exiting. It is known that both vehicles have an acceleration and deceleration magnitude of $2.5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. During the process of a car passing through the toll station, the distance traveled at a constant speed is...
2. Both cars decelerate from $15\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ and then accelerate back to a speed of exactly $15\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. Car 1 uses less time than Car 2 during this process.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the left blue dashed vertical line through A/B is the common deceleration line for both vehicles, the right blue dashed vertical line is the toll-station centerline, vehicle/object 1 is in the ETC lane and vehicle/object 2 is in the manual toll lane, both moving rightward. Use vehicle 2 to determine the fixed distance from AB to the toll centerline: it decelerates uniformly from 15 m/s to 0 with acceleration magnitude 2.5 m/s^2, so apply v^2 - v0^2 = 2as to get s = 45 m. For vehicle 1, compute the distance needed to decelerate from 15 m/s to 5 m/s under the same deceleration magnitude: s = (15^2 - 5^2)/(2·2.5) = 40 m. Therefore the remaining distance to the centerline, traveled at constant 5 m/s, is 45 - 40 = 5 m. Then compute times: vehicle 1 takes (15-5)/2.5 = 4 s to decelerate, 5/5 = 1 s at constant speed, and (15-5)/2.5 = 4 s to accelerate, total 9 s. Vehicle 2 takes 15/2.5 = 6 s to decelerate, 10 s paying, and 15/2.5 = 6 s to accelerate, total 22 s. The time saved by vehicle 1 is 22 - 9 = 13 s.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中有两条行驶通道，车辆均向右行驶。左侧蓝色竖直虚线经过 A、B，表示两车共同开始减速的减速线 AB；右侧蓝色竖直虚线表示收费站中心线。object 1 在 ETC Lane，object 2 在 Manual toll lane。

再推理：先用车辆 2 确定从减速线 AB 到收费站中心线的距离。车辆 2 从 15 m/s 匀减速到 0，减速度大小为 2.5 m/s²。由 v² - v0² = 2as，取运动方向为正，a = -2.5 m/s²：0² - 15² = 2(-2.5)s，所以 s = 45 m。

车辆 1 从 15 m/s 匀减速到 5 m/s，减速度大小同为 2.5 m/s²。由 5² - 15² = 2(-2.5)s，得 s = 40 m。因此车辆 1 减速到 5 m/s 后到收费站中心线的剩余距离为 45 - 40 = 5 m，这段就是匀速行驶距离。

计算时间：车辆 1 减速时间为 (15 - 5)/2.5 = 4 s，匀速通过 5 m 的时间为 5/5 = 1 s，再从 5 m/s 加速到 15 m/s 的时间为 (15 - 5)/2.5 = 4 s，所以车辆 1 总时间为 4 + 1 + 4 = 9 s。车辆 2 减速到停止的时间为 15/2.5 = 6 s，缴费停留 10 s，再加速到 15 m/s 的时间为 15/2.5 = 6 s，所以车辆 2 总时间为 6 + 10 + 6 = 22 s。车辆 1 比车辆 2 少用时间 22 - 9 = 13 s。

推理：按指定方法用速度—时间图像面积表示位移。车 2 从 15 m/s 匀减速到 0，加速度大小为 2.5 m/s^2，所以减速时间 t2减 = 15/2.5 = 6 s。其 v-t 图为三角形，AB 到中心线的距离为面积 S = 1/2 × 6 × 15 = 45 m。车 1 从 15 m/s 匀减速到 5 m/s，时间 t1减 = (15 - 5)/2.5 = 4 s。其减速阶段 v-t 图为梯形，位移 S1减 = ((15 + 5)/2) × 4 = 40 m。由于图中两车从 AB 到中心线的距离相同，均为 45 m，所以车 1 在减速到 5 m/s 后到中心线前还要匀速行驶 45 - 40 = 5 m。因此第 1 问匀速行驶距离为 5 m。车 1 匀速 5 m 的时间为 5/5 = 1 s，之后从 5 m/s 匀加速到 15 m/s 的时间为 (15 - 5)/2.5 = 4 s，所以车 1 总时间为 4 + 1 + 4 = 9 s。车 2 减速用 6 s，停车缴费 10 s，再从 0 匀加速到 15 m/s 用 15/2.5 = 6 s，所以车 2 总时间为 6 + 10 + 6 = 22 s。车 1 比车 2 少用 22 - 9 = 13 s。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This method is based on a velocity-time graph and area-under-curve interpretation, rather than directly applying the displacement equation segment by segment. It treats distances as graph areas and times as graph widths.
planner_metadata.image_role: Use the visual layout to see that the ETC and manual lanes share the same horizontal distance between the left AB dashed line and the right centerline, so the manual-lane stopping distance can calibrate the ETC-lane distance.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the described speed changes and waiting time: vehicle 1 changes 15→5→15 with a constant-speed middle part, while vehicle 2 changes 15→0, waits 10 s, then changes 0→15.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the velocity-time graph principle that displacement equals area under the v-t curve, and use uniform acceleration to convert speed changes into time intervals via Δt = Δv/a.

raw_record.original_question:
ETC is the abbreviation for the Electronic Toll Collection system on highways, which can speed up the passage of vehicles on highways. As shown in the figure, vehicles 1 and 2 both start with an initial velocity of $v_{0}=15\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ and travel in the same direction, taking the ETC lane and the manual toll lane respectively to exit the highway. Vehicle 1 starts to decelerate uniformly from the deceleration line AB, and when its speed reduces to $v=5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$, it continues to travel at a constant speed to the centerline of the toll station, then accelerates uniformly back to $15\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ before exiting. Vehicle 2 also starts to decelerate uniformly from the deceleration line AB, comes to a complete stop exactly at the centerline of the toll station, spends $10\mathrm{s}$ paying the toll, and then accelerates uniformly back to $15\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ before exiting. It is known that both vehicles have an acceleration and deceleration magnitude of $2.5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. During the process of a car passing through the toll station, the distance traveled at a constant speed is...
2. Both cars decelerate from $15\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ and then accelerate back to a speed of exactly $15\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. Car 1 uses less time than Car 2 during this process.
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: There are two driving lanes in the figure, and the vehicles are both traveling to the right. The blue vertical dashed line on the left passes through A and B, representing the deceleration line AB where the two vehicles jointly begin to decelerate; the blue vertical dashed line on the right represents the toll station centerline. object 1 is in ETC Lane, and object 2 is in Manual toll lane.

Then reason: First use vehicle 2 to determine the distance from deceleration line AB to the toll station centerline. Vehicle 2 uniformly decelerates from 15 m/s to 0, with a deceleration magnitude of 2.5 m/s². From v² - v0² = 2as, taking the direction of motion as positive, a = -2.5 m/s²: 0² - 15² = 2(-2.5)s, so s = 45 m.

Vehicle 1 uniformly decelerates from 15 m/s to 5 m/s, with the same deceleration magnitude of 2.5 m/s². From 5² - 15² = 2(-2.5)s, obtain s = 40 m. Therefore, after vehicle 1 decelerates to 5 m/s, the remaining distance to the toll station centerline is 45 - 40 = 5 m, and this section is the uniform-speed driving distance.

Calculate time: The deceleration time of vehicle 1 is (15 - 5)/2.5 = 4 s, the time to pass 5 m at uniform speed is 5/5 = 1 s, and the time to accelerate from 5 m/s to 15 m/s is (15 - 5)/2.5 = 4 s, so the total time for vehicle 1 is 4 + 1 + 4 = 9 s. The time for vehicle 2 to decelerate to a stop is 15/2.5 = 6 s, the toll payment stop is 10 s, and the time to accelerate to 15 m/s is 15/2.5 = 6 s, so the total time for vehicle 2 is 6 + 10 + 6 = 22 s. Vehicle 1 uses 22 - 9 = 13 s less time than vehicle 2.
